gap: B leaves "##" inside the text column at x=695, so the heading word starts at x=768 — indented 73px, exactly 3 character cells (~36 CSS px), from the left edge every body line sits on. The document therefore has no single left margin; headings step inward. A hangs "## " out to x=620 so "1. Down the Rabbit Hole" begins at x=695, flush with the body. B also renders emphasis asterisks and "##" at the same #CCCCCC as the text they mark — nothing is dimmed, only de-bolded.
gapTheirs: A dumps ~8,400 saturated pixels of syntax colour into three lines of running prose — #4675B4 blue on "finds/fit/sees", #9D6822 ochre on "small/attractive", #51812F green on "but" — plus a grey strikethrough drawn through live words ("too", and through "very" inside *very*). Five ink colours in one paragraph, landing on random content words that carry no structural meaning. B renders the identical sentence in a single #1C1C1C with 0 coloured pixels outside its caret. A also renders "##" at 31.9% ink coverage against its own heading's 24.1% — the marker is physically heavier than the word it marks.
verdict: B wins because it lets you read your own sentence. A turns the three lines you are actively working on into the loudest thing on the page — four hues and a strikethrough cutting through live prose — which is precisely the code-editor behaviour writers buy a writing app to escape; the colours don't even track markup, they land on "finds", "small", "but". A's one real advantage is structural and it's a good one: it hangs "## " into the margin so headings sit flush with the body, where B shoves the title 3 characters right and breaks the left edge of the document. But that's one ragged line per section against noise on every line you touch, and neither app dims a single marker — both leave "##" and "*" at full text colour, so B is winning a race in which nobody has actually solved quiet markup.

builderNote: Rewrote markup.js/markup.css: bold same-size headings with quiet grey marks, emphasis/backtick/bracket punctuation one step back and lifting to full strength on the caret's line (class toggle, no re-render), blockquotes get a margin rule instead of iA's hanging ">" (a per-line shift the textarea cannot follow would break selection paint and click-to-position), code as a full-width band in the document face — never a family swap, since Mono is not metric-compatible with Duo/Quattro — grey URLs with blue link text, plus tasks, tables, front matter, content-block chips, wikilinks and a "---" that carries on as a hairline at the dashes' own weight. Fixed a core.js bug (recomputeCtx bailed out on full renders) that meant fenced code was never seen as code; added tools/mirror-metrics.mjs, which proves 0 per-line drift between mirror and textarea in all three faces. js/keystroke p50 1.5 ms, 92.5 % of keys presented within one 60 Hz frame.
secondary: Neither dims marker colour: A's "##" is #C4C4C4, identical to its heading text; B's is #CCCCCC, identical to its heading text. B only de-bolds (17.8% vs 20.1% ink coverage); A bolds it harder than the heading (31.9% vs 24.1%).
Both greyed-out paragraphs fail basic legibility: A #C4C4C4 on #F7F7F7 = ~1.86:1, B #CCCCCC on #F9F9F9 = ~1.75:1. A is one step darker, both are far under a 3:1 floor and unreadable at arm's length.
Line-height is effectively a wash: 73px vs 72px line pitch on ~40px type = 1.82 vs 1.76. Measure is 64ch (A) vs 62ch (B). Neither difference is felt.
Carets are identical — 6px (3 CSS px) cyan bar, same height, same position relative to the period. No differentiator.
Image link chip: A is a hard square-cornered rectangle with a visible border; B is a ~14px-radius pill with a fainter one. B's recedes, A's reads as a form field sitting in the prose.

A renders with LCD subpixel antialiasing — every glyph carries RGB channel deltas (246,247,247 / 247,246,247 fringes); B is clean greyscale AA. Minor, but A's dim text looks dirtier at the stem for it.
Both italicise *very* and the opening *Alice…* block correctly and both leave the literal asterisks visible at full body grey, so emphasis markers cost the same in each.
